description: Implementation of a Programme to minimize the damages caused to crop cultivation and livelihood by wild animals roaming in human settlements and agricultural lands
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2026-03-03 (Subject to Confirmation at the next Meeting)
decision_details_body: - Crop damages caused by wild animals such as elephants, wild boars, monkeys, toque macaques, giant squirrels and peacocks roaming around human settlements and cultivated lands have severely impacted rural agricultural livelihoods and food security in the country. In addition, there are frequent reports of wildlife-human conflicts and property damages, and serious social and economic problems have also arisen. Therefore, the Ministry of Agriculture, Livestock, Land and Irrigation has prepared a comprehensive programme based on the views of all stakeholders, including the public, the university community, farmer organizations, environmentalists, NGOs dealing with environmental issues, the Department of Agriculture, the Department of Agrarian Development, and other relevant institutions, to manage damages to crops and harm to human life caused by wild animals. Taking into account the matters presented by the Minister of Agriculture, Livestock, Land and Irrigation in this regard, the Cabinet decided to appoint a Ministerial Committee under the Chairmanship of the Minister of Agriculture, Livestock, Land and Irrigation and with the participation of other relevant Ministers to review the proposals included in the said programme and submit appropriate recommendations on how to implement the said programme, including new proposals that are further identified.
